name: iShares Semiconductor ETF
note: ETF — exception to standard no-ETF rule; included because SOXX is a central subject of this bookmark.
blurb: The iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) tracks the ICE Semiconductor Index, a modified market-capitalisation-weighted benchmark of 34 companies spanning the full semiconductor value chain: chip designers (fabless), integrated device manufacturers, equipment makers, and electronic design automation software firms. BlackRock launched the fund in 2001 under ticker SOXX (previously SOXX tracked the PHLX SOX index). A distinctive capping rule limits the top five holdings to a maximum 8% weight and all others to 4%, preventing any single mega-cap from dominating the basket. As of May 2026 the fund's top ten holdings are AMD (8.10%), Broadcom (7.95%), Micron Technology (7.93%), NVIDIA (6.75%), Intel (6.58%), Marvell Technology (6.09%), Applied Materials (4.70%), Monolithic Power Systems (4.18%), Texas Instruments (3.99%), and NXP Semiconductors (3.92%) — collectively 60% of a $30 billion AUM. Expense ratio: 0.35% annually. SOXX is widely used as a proxy for the broader semiconductor cycle and is the most closely watched chip-sector ETF alongside the VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH).
recent: SOXX posted its largest monthly return in the fund's 25-year history in April 2026, gaining approximately 40% — a pace not seen since the dot-com peak of February 2000. The rally was broad-based rather than Nvidia-driven: Intel surged 131%, AMD gained ~75%, Marvell exceeded 64%, Credo Technology rose 88%, and Astera Labs 84%, while Nvidia gained a comparatively modest 22%. SOXX's capping methodology meant it benefited fully from breadth rotation, outpacing SMH (which gained 32%) whose 18% Nvidia weight acted as a relative drag. From its March 30 trough of ~$310 to its April 23 high near $463, SOXX logged 17 consecutive up days — its longest ever winning streak. Year-to-date through early May 2026, SOXX is up roughly 50%. RSI readings above 80 signal technically overbought conditions. The AI-infrastructure buildout and tariff exemptions on advanced semiconductors were primary fundamental catalysts.
